claim: The First Amendment right of access to governmental proceedings encompasses a right to hear the sounds of executions in their entirety, and restrictions on press access—but not general public access—to those sounds impermissibly burden that right, while an inmates' right-of-access-to-the-courts claim that fails as a matter of law may be dismissed without leave to amend.
initial_reasoning: 938 F.3d 1069 (Coalition v. Ryan) expressly holds that the First Amendment right of access to governmental proceedings includes a right to hear the sounds of executions in their entirety, that restrictions on press access (but not general public access) to those sounds impermissibly burden that right, and that an inmate’s right‑of‑access‑to‑the‑courts claim that fails as a matter of law may be dismissed without leave to amend.
